card: Adds an -ipcconnect command-line option to bitcoin-gui, enabling it to connect over IPC to an existing background bitcoin-node process rather than spawning a new node child process. This allows users of multiprocess builds to run a persistent node daemon and attach or detach GUI instances independently. The PR is part of the larger multiprocess separation project (#28722). It depends on #10102, #19460, and #29409, with only the final commit belonging specifically to this pull request.

enables: Process separation milestone (#28722), and future support for connecting the GUI directly to separate wallet processes

evidence: PR description: 'This allows the GUI to be started and stopped independently of the node. By default with this change, bitcoin-gui will check if a <datadir>/sockets/node.sock socket exists and try to connect to that. If that doesn't work, it will spawn a new node process and start up the same way it did before this PR.'
Author notes part of the tracking project for process separation: 'This PR is part of the process separation project (#28722).'
problem: In multiprocess builds, `bitcoin-gui` unconditionally spawns and manages its own internal `bitcoin-node` child process. Users cannot leave a persistent node daemon running in the background and connect or disconnect GUI sessions on demand.
scope_notes: This PR is stacked on top of #10102, #29409, and #19460. Only the top commit (80bebc1624) is unique to this PR; the remaining commits in the diff include libmultiprocess subtree updates, Cap'n Proto interface wrappers, and changes to btcsignals lifetime semantics. Multiprocess features are only compiled when configured with `--enable-multiprocess`.
summary: Adds an `-ipcconnect` option to `bitcoin-gui`, allowing it to attach to an already running `bitcoin-node` IPC socket rather than spawning a new node subprocess. It supports `-ipcconnect=auto` by default to connect to an existing node socket if present or spawn one otherwise, as well as explicit socket paths with `unix:<path>`.
